properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-20, immediately after #262 made reflow2's module graph acyclic. Lift the SAME acyclic import edges up to the 8 declared subsystems, using each Component's CONTAINS placement, and TWO CYCLES APPEAR.

=== THE RESULT ===

  MODULES: 53 + 25, zero cycles at top-module and file granularity. Confirmed.
  SUBSYSTEMS: 8 declared, and the graph over them has TWO cycles.

  1) sys:store <-> sys:vocabulary
       store -> vocabulary via graph->nodes, graph->schema, export->nodes
       vocabulary -> store via flow->graph, vocabulary->graph

  2) sys:coherence-loop <-> sys:time-history
       coherence-loop -> time-history via artifact->temporal, confirm->temporal
       time-history -> coherence-loop via compare->report        <- ONE back-edge

=== WHY THIS IS THE POINT, NOT A CURIOSITY ===

A wall you can hand a change to is a wall traffic crosses in ONE direction. At a mutually coupled boundary there is nothing for a blast radius to stop at, so severability at sys:store and sys:vocabulary is not merely unmeasured - it is FALSE. dec:idea-stated-module-function-is-what-makes-failure-mode-testing-derivable and the flo2 change-propagation chain both assume walls exist to follow; at two of the eight, they do not.

The insight already recorded - MODULARIZATION IS ABOUT ADDING WALLS, NOT EDGES - now has its first concrete instance, and the walls in question are already declared. They just do not hold.

=== THE ROOT CAUSE IS PLACEMENT, NOT CODE ===

Cycle 1 is not a defect in the source. The kernel is four modules that everything sits on - nodes (46 of 52 modules transitively depend on it), provenance (44), schema (43), graph (42) - and the declared decomposition CUTS IT IN HALF:

  cmp:nodes  -> sys:vocabulary        cmp:graph      -> sys:store
  cmp:schema -> sys:vocabulary        cmp:provenance -> sys:store

graph reads nodes and schema; vocabulary and flow read graph. Any bisection of a mutually-dependent kernel produces a cycle at the level above it, whatever the code does. PUT ALL FOUR ON ONE SIDE AND CYCLE 1 CEASES TO EXIST WITHOUT TOUCHING A LINE OF RUST. cmp:identity - code degree 5, 44 of 52 modules downstream - is placed in NO subsystem at all, which is the same mistake in its most complete form.

Cycle 2 has the shape all three of #262's cycles had: one back-edge, compare->report. It is one honest question - does comparing two designs need the REPORT layer, or a narrower thing report also uses - not a restructuring.

=== AND REFLOW2 CANNOT SEE ANY OF IT ===

reflow2 HAS a circular-dependency detector and it is right to report none, because the design holds exactly TWO coupling edges touching any of the 8 subsystems, and both are sys:store CONSUMES an external interface. Zero subsystem-to-subsystem edges exist, so the detector has nothing to run on. The green reads as 'your subsystems are acyclic'; it means 'your subsystems have no modelled coupling'. Those are opposite facts wearing the same answer, and this is the third instance in three days of the same pattern: THE MECHANISM EXISTS, IS TESTED, AND IS UNREACHABLE FROM WHERE THE PERSON IS STUCK.

FOR AN ARBITRARY USER'S PROJECT that is the whole risk: a decomposition is declared once, early, when it is cheapest to get wrong, and every later answer about severability and blast radius is computed through it. Nothing today checks a declared decomposition against the coupling it is supposed to contain.

=== METHOD ===

Import edges from crates/*/src/**.rs, comments and string literals stripped, mapped module-leaf-name to Component id to CONTAINS parent; Tarjan over the induced subsystem graph. 42 of 56 Components are placed in a subsystem; 39 of those name a module present in the code graph. Of the code edges with both ends placed, 27 stay inside a subsystem and 67 cross - but crossing is not itself a fault, since a foundation layer is SUPPOSED to be depended on. Only the two-way crossings are, and there are two.
